finding.claim: GET /users has no authentication and trusts the caller-supplied org query parameter, so any unauthenticated client can enumerate user ids and names for any org (cross-tenant disclosure).
finding.source: req.query.org (db.js:9), reachable via unauthenticated GET /users on port 3002
finding.sink: req.pg.query SELECT id, name FROM users WHERE org = $1 (db.js:9), response returned via res.json(rows) (db.js:10)

trace.note: Route registered directly on app with no auth middleware; app has no app.use guards in this file
org taken from req.query and bound as parameter $1; query is parameterized so no SQLi, but no caller identity is compared to org
All matching id and name rows returned to the caller

finding.guards_checked: Parameterized SQL (no SQL injection). No auth guard on route (checklist A1). No tenant/owner comparison possible since no caller identity exists (A2). req.pg is set outside this file; if upstream middleware authenticates requests the impact narrows to any authenticated user reading any org, which could not be verified. Confidence medium.

verdict.guard_found: none. The only controls are parameterized SQL at db.js:9, which blocks SQL injection but not cross-tenant access, and no auth middleware or app.use guard exists in db.js (the file is the only one in the directory). The path-containment check at db.js:15 belongs to /file, not /users.
verdict.reason: The route at db.js:8 has no auth check, db.js:9 binds the caller-supplied req.query.org straight into the query with no comparison to any caller identity, and db.js:10 returns every matching id and name, so an anonymous client on port 3002 can enumerate any org's users. The candidate's caveat holds: req.pg is set outside this file, but no upstream auth exists in the provided code, so the finding stands as written.
